title: A pyramid of energy
caption: Energy is lost at every step of a food chain as heat from respiration, uneaten parts, faeces and excretion, so typically only about 10% passes to the next trophic level. A pyramid of energy is therefore always upright, and food chains rarely have more than four or five links. The figures are illustrative.
alt: A four-level pyramid on a log scale: producers 10,000, primary consumers 1,000, secondary consumers 100 and tertiary consumers 10 kilojoules per square metre per year, each level a tenth of the one below.
description: Producers capture 10,000 kJ per m² per year (illustrative).
Primary consumers receive about 10% of that: 1,000.
At every step about 90% is lost as heat, in faeces or excretion, or left uneaten.
Energy is never recycled: it leaves the ecosystem as heat.
